name: Kung Fu Girl
notes: Transcribed from C:/rw/corpus/kfg (MUGEN/Ikemen 1.0 CNS): 25 of the character's 43 attacking states.
Frame counts derive from Kung Fu Girl.air element durations and each HitDef's AnimElem trigger; hitstun from ground.hittime.

startup = the first tick on which a Clsn1 box exists AND a HitDef has been registered. The two disagree on exactly two moves in this corpus: stand_hp_far (HitDef at element 4 = tick 6, first Clsn1 at element 5 = tick 8) and super_palm (first Clsn1 at element 4 = tick 9, HitDef at element 5 = tick 11). Both take the later tick.

Every cancel delay is DERIVED, not assumed zero. KFG's chain and special cancels are gated on var(5), whose opening frame is authored per source state as AnimElemTime(N) >= 0 in System.cns:3009-3025, so delay = (tick element N begins) - startup. Only the super cancel and palm -> EX palm are true cancels at delay 0, because they are gated on movecontact/movehit alone.
Pushback is ESTIMATED as |ground.velocity| * ground.slidetime / 2. MUGEN records a velocity, never a displacement.

Hitstun decay is 'none' because MUGEN has none. The draft schema's house rule (linear 2/10) was authored and measured first: its floor of 10 exceeds stand_lp's 9 frames of hitstun and would RAISE it, and even corrected to 6 it flipped the verdict to TERMINATING with 6 of 134 cancels usable, because both implementations evaluate every edge at the settled hitstun. See decay.engine.house_rule_measured_and_rejected.

Juggle is DEAD DATA in this character: [Data] airjuggle = 0 (System.cns:7) and AssertSpecial nojugglecheck (System.cns:2590-2593) turn MUGEN's juggle system off, so Supers.cns:6's juggle = 4 is never read. The real limiter is the character's own var(15)/var(16) counters gating every normal's HitDef, which schema v1 cannot express.
Not transcribed: throw (800), Heavy Smash (500), the six jumping normals (600-651), the medium and strong palm and knee variants, EX Knee (1130) and the EX Shuffle chain (1330-1333).

engine.derivation: DERIVED, in the sense that the source says nothing: MUGEN 1.0 has no global hitstun decay. Every HitDef states an absolute ground.hittime and no controller reduces it as a combo runs. 'none' is the truthful transcription and, like 'linear', it is pure integer arithmetic in both implementations (model.py:257-259, comboprover.hpp:74-75), so it closes ARCHITECTURE D8's hitstun gap outright. 'multiplicative' remains forbidden.
engine.house_rule_measured_and_rejected: The draft schema's house rule (linear, step 2, floor 10) was authored and run. Two findings. (1) The floor is WRONG AT 10 for this character: model.py:260 and comboprover.hpp:81 compute max(floor, base - step*n), so a floor above a move's base hitstun RAISES it, and stand_lp's ground.hittime is 9 (Normal.cns:48). A floor must never exceed the smallest hitstun in the file. (2) Even with the floor corrected to 6, the verdict flipped to TERMINATING with only 6 of 134 authored cancels usable. That is not a fact about Kung Fu Girl: both implementations evaluate every edge at the SETTLED hitstun (comboprover.hpp:336-339, model.py settling_index), which here is 14 hits, so a 2-frames-per-hit rule collapses every move to the floor and reports 128 real cancels as dead. A decay rule invented for a character that has none deletes the character. Recorded because it is the single most dangerous authoring mistake this schema permits.

engine.derivation: 1 unit = 10 MUGEN power. Every power value in this transcription -- 10, 20, 30, 40, 80, 120 and 1000 (Normal.cns:9,33,79,107,353,388; Specials.cns:9,337; Supers.cns:23) -- is a multiple of 10, so 1/100 of a 1000-power bar is exact and no loader ever rounds.
engine.ceiling_warning: comboprover.hpp carries no ceilings (Character :148-174) and nonNegative :264-269 hardcodes floor 0, while model.py:192 and termination.py:200,245,252 clamp. The ~200-line adapter must clamp in its own search loop, or the editor panel and the offline run search different state spaces.

engine.derivation: DECLARED BUT INERT for Kung Fu Girl. [Data] airjuggle = 0 (System.cns:7) and AssertSpecial nojugglecheck (System.cns:2590-2593) disable MUGEN's juggle system outright, so Supers.cns:6's juggle = 4 is never read and no move here spends a point. Declared anyway so the positional ResourceVec comboprover.hpp keys on (:56, :128-129, :152) has the same order in all three Phase-0 characters. The paper's own importer would read juggle -4 / guard 4 on super_palm (mugen_cns.py:582-585); for this character that would be fabricated.
engine.real_limiter: var(15) counts hits since the defender was last grounded and var(16) flags a hit-fall state (System.cns:2611-2666); every normal's HitDef is gated on !var(16) && var(15) < 1. See engine.hit_rules and each normal's engine.hit_condition.

cancels.label: Kung Fu Palm cancelled into EX Kung Fu Palm

engine.source: corpus/kfg/Kung Fu Girl.cmd:613 (trigger3 = (Stateno=[1000,1020]) && Movehit; no var(5), so delay 0)

cancels.caveat: window is AnimElemTime(5) >= 0 && AnimElemTime(8) < 0 (Specials.cns:767): animation 1100 element 5 begins on tick 15 and element 8 on tick 26, so the window is ticks 15-25 and the delay is 15 - 7 = 8. MUGEN operator precedence makes Specials.cns:769 parse as (movehit && a) || b || c, so the b and c buttons reach it on whiff too; authored on-hit, which is the evident intent.
cancels.label: Kung Fu Knee into its follow-up kick

cancels.caveat: window AnimElemTime(3) > 0 && AnimElemTime(8) < 0: element 3 begins on tick 6 so the strict > 0 opens it on tick 7, one frame after the move connects. No contact is required, hence on=always.

cancels.caveat: window AnimElemTime(3) > 0 && AnimElemTime(8) < 0: element 3 begins on tick 5, so the window opens on tick 6. No contact required, hence on=always.

constants.source: corpus/kfg/System.cns:2-49 -- life 1000, walk.fwd 3, walk.back -2.8, run.fwd 5.7, run.back -5.1, jump.neu 0,-11, yaccel .58, stand.friction .85, crouch.friction .82, airjump.num 0, ground.back/front 13, height 60, attack.dist 160

engine.derivation_legend: Each move's engine.derivation is one line of provenance, fields in this order, all paths relative to corpus/kfg/: <cns>:<statedef line> | HitDef :<line> AnimElem=<n> (gives startup) | dmg :<line> | ground.hittime :<line> (gives hitstun) | slidetime,velocity :<lines> (the two inputs to the ESTIMATED pushback, |vel|*slide/2 px) | poweradd :<line> + getpower :<line> = <MUGEN power> = <schema units at 10 power per unit> | anim <id> .air:<Begin Action line> (element durations give active and recovery = total-startup-active+1, mugen_cns.py:560-561) | Clsn1 <px> .air:<line> (x2 of the attack box, gives reach in units of 100px) | var(5) opening element, System.cns line, tick, and the delay arithmetic for every cancel out of the move.

chain.authored_as: trigger2 = (stateno=A||stateno=B||...) && var(5) && Movehit, one row per TARGET in [Statedef -1] of Kung Fu Girl.cmd. The per-edge engine.source cites the exact trigger2 line.
chain.delay_rule: var(5) opens at AnimElemTime(N) >= 0 && Movecontact, authored per SOURCE state in System.cns:3009-3025; delay = (tick element N begins) - source.startup. Each move's engine.derivation carries its own N, tick and arithmetic.
chain.caveat: no importer can evaluate var(5) without reading the System.cns:3009-3025 table; certain=false records that.

special.authored_as: trigger2 = var(5), with no stateno restriction, on each special's row in [Statedef -1]: Kung Fu Girl.cmd:676 (palm), :640 (knee), :649 (shuffle), :613 (EX palm). Every state with a var(5) row is therefore a source -- all 16 of them, and NOT crouch_hk (450), which has no row.
special.delay_rule: same var(5) rule as the chain family.
special.caveat: var(5) is set on Movecontact (System.cns:3009-3025), i.e. hit OR block. The prover's `on` vocabulary has no hit-or-block, so only the on-hit half is authored; four representative on-block edges are included to show the shape.

special_block.authored_as: the on-block half of the `special` family, four representative edges only. See that family's caveat.

super.authored_as: one row, Kung Fu Girl.cmd:744-750: triggerall power >= 1000; trigger2 = statetype != A && hitdefattr = SC,NA,SA,HA && stateno != [3000,3050) && movecontact. This is the [Statedef -1]-style global transition ARCHITECTURE Phase 5 names: 'from any attack that has already connected'. v1 has no way to say it once, so it is expanded to 24 edges, one per attacking move.
super.delay_rule: delay 0. Gated on movecontact alone, not var(5), so it is a true cancel on the connecting frame.

engine.cancel_note: An edge carrying engine.family inherits that family's condition, delay rule, certainty and caveat; its engine.source cites the one line that differs. Edges with no family carry all four themselves. This keeps 122 homogeneous edges from repeating the same 400 characters.
engine.anim_note: Per-move engine.anim_id names the Begin Action in Kung Fu Girl.air (cited in engine.derivation). The per-frame box arrays the full schema calls for -- 4 x int16 sub-units for hit/hurt/push, plus sprite refs and events -- are NOT transcribed here: 25 moves x ~10 elements x ~3 boxes is a hitbox-editor job (ARCHITECTURE Phase 3), and no prover field depends on them. The shape was validated on stand_lp against .air:746-764 during the schema draft.

hit_rules.source: corpus/kfg/Normal.cns:27, and the identical trigger on every other normal's HitDef: trigger1 = !var(16) && var(15) < 1
hit_rules.note: A CHARACTER-LEVEL rule with no home in schema v1. It is one row of data, identical on all 17 normals, so it is counted once as a character-level schema gap rather than 17 times as a per-move escape hatch. Recorded here so Phase 5 designs its grammar from what a real character needs; today the engine would hard-code it.
hit_rules.schema_gap: v1 needs a move-level hit_condition enum (or a character-level hit rule table) taking a predicate over the DEFENDER's state. This is the single largest gap the transcription found by move count.

schema_fields_that_would_close_it: move.engine.motion[] -- the attacker's own per-frame velocity/position track (closes 8 moves)
move.engine.hit_profiles[] -- a second HitDef with its own box, damage and stun, selected by whether the first whiffed (closes 1 move)
move.engine.anim.frames[].invuln -- per-frame invulnerability by attack attribute, same shape as the box arrays (closes 1 move)
move.engine.transitions[].on_land -- a physics-state transition kind alongside the frame-indexed ones (closes 2 moves, both already counted)
move.hit_condition / engine.hit_rules -- a predicate over the DEFENDER's state (closes the 1 character-level gap covering all 17 normals)
fit.note: Every [P] field of all 25 moves was derived from the corpus with no gap, so the fragment the prover decides over fits this character completely: prover_visible_losses is 0. The escape hatches counted here are ALL engine-side (Phase 3) and NONE of them needs C++ or an expression language to say what a move DOES -- six named data fields close every one, and they are listed above. The two flagged runtime_condition (the proximity-variant selector and the landing predicate) each become declarative with one predicate.
known_losses: Random-gated controllers (Normal.cns:15, AnimElem = 1 && Random < 300) cannot exist in a deterministic sim; those sounds are made unconditional.

getpower is read here but the paper's own importer ignores it (mugen_cns.py:592-600), so our meter gains are 4-5x a mugen_cns import of the same character. givepower (the defender's meter) has no home in a single-character model at all.

MUGEN's Movecontact means hit OR block. The prover's on vocabulary is hit|block|whiff|always with no hit-or-block, so the 64 special-cancel edges are authored on-hit (the verdict-relevant half) plus four representative on-block edges. Authoring the block half in full would double the cancel count and change no verdict.

var(5)'s first trigger, (stateno = [200,699]) && Time <= 2 (System.cns:3009), gives every normal a 3-frame kara-cancel into a special with no contact required. That is a cancel at NEGATIVE delay from the connecting frame and model.py:167-170 rejects delay < 0, so it is documented rather than authored.
Pushback is estimated from velocity * slidetime / 2. MUGEN records no displacement, and this is the number the midscreen verdict turns on.
Hitstop (pausetime, 6 to 15 ticks per move) freezes attacker and defender together, so it cancels out of the frame-advantage arithmetic and is not modelled in the [P] fields.
Multi-hit moves collapse to one record: super_palm's three HitDefs (Supers.cns:82,105) become one 219-damage hit, and chop's alternate far HitDef (Normal.cns:223) is dropped.
18 of the character's 43 attacking states were not transcribed.
